sense: a skilled craftsman; an expert in an art

terms.gloss: a master of an art, a skilled craftsman
evidence: Liv. 42.3: reponendārum nēmō artifex inīre ratiōnem potuit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: One who has mastered an art, from ars and faciō; Lewis & Short sets it against opifex, the worker in the humbler crafts. It also means an artist or performer (artificēs scaenicī), and, of a person, a past master at something, even at mischief. For the one who does it for a living, see professional.

terms.gloss: a master, the one in charge; a teacher
evidence: Col. 1.18: magister operārum, an overseer (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 1.244: puerī apud magistrōs exercentur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The head of something (a ship, a company, a feast, a team of workmen) and the teacher of a skill: so the master with apprentices, who directs and teaches. Its everyday sense is teacher (see teacher); for mastery of the skill itself, artifex.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.150: opificēs omnēs in sordidā arte versantur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The maker in a manual craft; with a word for the craft, a master of it: opifex verbōrum (Cic. Tusc. 5.34).

phrases.latin: Sed assuēscere oportet: nēmō nāscitur artifex.
phrases.english: But you have to get used to it: nobody is born a master.
phrases.source: Erasm. Coll., Lūsus puerīlēs, Natātiō, I 44 (not classical)

phrases.latin: reponendārum nēmō artifex inīre ratiōnem potuit
phrases.english: no master builder could work out how to put the tiles back
